stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Cross-platform live preview (GO, UP, MX) involves real-time rendering, content security, and cross-platform complexity. Openspec must elaborate requirements first; speckit then hardens for testability, security, and edge cases.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — CMS live preview does not exist in the codebase. ContentstackProvider is the single injection point for all content; enhancing it is the minimal-integration path. ACs are empty so VCs derive from the description and the located fix-site analysis. Contentstack.io is unreachable at test time; VCs are phrased to the boundary of our code.

Openspec produced empty ACs, so all criteria are new. ACs are derived solely from the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the three target sites (GO, UP, MX), and the four key file paths (ContentstackContext, contentCard, ContentstackLink, useContent). File contents were NOT available for review, which limits precision — for example, the exact fields on contentCard and the exact API of useContent are assumed from naming conventions. If the actual interfaces differ significantly, some ACs (especially AC-5, AC-7, AC-8) may need adjustment. AC-3 addresses security (no preview data leak in production). AC-2, AC-11, AC-12 address error-handling and resilience. AC-9 addresses accessibility for dynamic content updates. AC-10 addresses cross-site consistency. AC-4 and AC-5 address edge cases around partial and concurrent updates.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Verification criteria are observable and testable — all four VCs describe concrete, automatable behaviors (hash-param detection, draft rendering, live update without reload, fallback to published, multi-field batch update). Both agents added non-overlapping value: openspec identified the novel capability and ContentstackProvider as the single injection point, noting Contentstack.io is unreachable at test time so VCs are phrased to the code boundary; speckit then hardened for security (preview data leak), error handling, accessibility, and cross-site consistency. Two concerns require human attention. (1) Cross-codeline path mismatch: the story declares src/context/ContentstackContext.tsx, but upexpress resolves to src/context/ContentstackContext.ts (extension variant .tsx→.ts) and metrolinx resolves to src/context/contentstackContext.tsx (case variant Contentstack→contentstack). Both are marked resolved, not missing, and the per-codeline resolved array provides the actual paths — but a writer sent the declared path on those two codelines would fail. The runner must confirm it passes per-codeline actual paths to the writer. (2) VC coverage gap: speckit's notes reference ACs up to AC-12 covering security (AC-3), error handling (AC-2, AC-11, AC-12), accessibility (AC-9), cross-site consistency (AC-10), and edge cases (AC-4, AC-5) — but only 4 verification criteria are present. While empty acceptanceCriteria is expected for brownfield, the VCs are the observable checks and they do not cover the security, accessibility, or error-handling aspects speckit claims to have contributed. A human should confirm whether the 4 VCs sufficiently cover the story's risk surface or whether additional VCs should be promoted from speckit's notes into verificationCriteria.
